title: runtime: annotate logs/traces with quant_profile_id + resolution outcome
author: Noah Patel
release_notes: Runtime request logs and traces now include quant_profile_id and quant_profile_resolution (applied|fallback|disabled) to improve debuggability during route-level quantization rollouts.
description: Context: With route-level quantization profiles (ENG-5816) we need a deterministic, low-friction way to answer: (a) which profile was requested/resolved for a given request, and (b) whether the runtime actually applied it vs fell back to baseline. We already emit aggregate metrics (see pr-18463) but oncall/support and design partners are repeatedly asking for request-level attribution in logs/traces. This PR adds structured log fields and OpenTelemetry span attributes for quant_profile_id and resolution outcome across the request lifecycle. What’s included: 1) Structured request logs: add fields `quant_profile_id` (string) and `quant_profile_resolution` (enum: applied|fallback|disabled). For fallback paths we also emit `quant_profile_fallback_reason` (enum) to avoid forcing operators to infer from error text. 2) Tracing: set OTel attributes on the request root span (and propagate to child spans via context) `redwood.quant.profile_id` and `redwood.quant.resolution`. We intentionally do not add per-token or per-layer annotations. 3) Determinism: values are populated from the post-policy resolved profile ref that is already pinned in the request context; we do not re-query registry/policy during logging. 4) Performance/safety: annotations are added to the existing structured logger payload; no additional allocations on hot decode loop; profile_id is bounded (registry-signed IDs) and should not introduce unbounded cardinality beyond expected profile versions. Example: quant enabled + applied: {"request_id":"req_...","route":"chat-prod","model":"llama-3.1-70b","quant_profile_id":"qpl_llama-3.1-70b_int8_v3","quant_profile_resolution":"applied"}. Quant enabled but incompatible -> fallback: {"request_id":"req_...","quant_profile_id":"qpl_llama-3.1-70b_int8_v3","quant_profile_resolution":"fallback","quant_profile_fallback_reason":"incompatible_hardware"}. Quant feature off / no ref configured: {"request_id":"req_...","quant_profile_id":"","quant_profile_resolution":"disabled"}. Notes: This is intentionally scoped to annotation only (no new dashboards). Downstream dashboards/alerts will key off these fields via existing log-based metrics work in ENG-5817. Testing: unit tests for resolution mapping + OTel attribute propagation; integration test ensures log payload contains fields for applied/fallback/disabled without changing existing log schema for other requests.
commits: runtime/obs: plumb quant profile resolution into RequestContext
runtime/tracing: set OTel attributes on root span for quant profile
runtime: add fallback reason enum + mapping
tests: coverage for log payload + trace attributes
conversation: Hiro Tanaka (review): Can we guarantee we annotate the span after resolution but before decode starts? Want to be sure child spans inherit attributes for kernel selection profiling.

Noah Patel (author): Yep—attributes are set on the request root span right after policy resolution and before engine dispatch. Child spans read from the request context. Added a regression test to assert attribute presence on decode span too.

Caleb Johnson (review): Please prefix the OTel attribute keys with a stable namespace (we’ve been using `redwood.*`). Also, avoid `profile_ref` terminology in logs—customers keep asking for `quant_profile_id` specifically.

Noah Patel (author): Updated keys to `redwood.quant.profile_id` + `redwood.quant.resolution` and standardized field name to `quant_profile_id` everywhere. Left internal `profile_ref` in code comments only.
Mina Haddad (review): For fallback, can we include a reason code? Otherwise it’s hard to distinguish incompatible hardware vs max context vs artifact fetch failure.

Noah Patel (author): Added `quant_profile_fallback_reason` with a small enum (incompatible_hardware, incompatible_model, max_context_exceeded, artifact_unavailable, kill_switch_enabled, unknown). The runtime already has these branches; this just surfaces the classification.
Connor O'Brien (review): Any concerns about cardinality in log-based metrics if profile_id is high-cardinality?

Noah Patel (author): Profile IDs are versioned but expected to be low (single digits per model family). We also emit resolution even when profile_id empty (disabled) so we can measure baseline share without grouping by ID.
Hiro Tanaka (approve): LGTM after the decode span assertion. Thanks for keeping this out of the hot loop.
Caleb Johnson (approve): Approved. Attribute naming and schema update look good.
Mina Haddad (approve): Approved. Reason codes will help a lot for routing triage.
